results.reason: Issue 3 cites SA §13.2. It notes Norvane may assign 'to any third party' with no notice while Calder Ridge needs consent, explains the risk to drawings and supply continuity, and proposes mutual consent plus a bar on assignment to a competitor.

Issue 3 cites SA §13.3, describes the consent requirement and Norvane's termination right, and explains the leverage this gives Norvane over a sale or merger. It recommends deleting the clause or limiting it to competitor acquirers. The memo treats the sale as possible rather than pending, but it still addresses the impact on a sale.

Issue 4 identifies OF §2.2 (successive 3-year renewals unless notice is given 30 days before expiry), explains the lock-in risk, and recommends one-year renewals, 90-day notice, and a supplier reminder notice.
Issue 1 notes that §9.3 exempts only Calder Ridge's indemnity from the cap, while Norvane's indemnity stays capped. It recommends a mutual, narrowed carve-out and a narrower §10.1.
The memo correctly states the cap as fees paid in the prior 12 months (§9.1), Delaware law (§12.1), and a 3-year Initial Term from March 1, 2026.
The memo correctly states the SA §1.3 order of precedence (SA, then OF, then Sched.). It applies this to the renewal conflict, where SA §2.1 controls over OF §2.2, and to the invoice timing conflict.
The priority table ranks the indemnity issue Critical (#1) and change of control High (#3), both ahead of the Medium and Low issues.
Each issue has a Where, a Why it matters, and a Fix with proposed language. A separate Business Questions section at the end lists items needing client input.

The memo treats the Specifications Schedule as a source of significant problems. It ranks the OF/Schedule product mismatch as Critical Issue #2 and also flags the Schedule's AQL sampling, the §7.3 rejection timing, and the missing head standards.
